body_markdown:
A new generation of BMW 3 Series[is here](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/new-bmw-3-series-sheds-camo-reveals-specs-and-prices/) . While some may be most curious about the fully electric model in the modern “Neue Klasse” era, and others reserving their excitement for the next M3, we are most excited for the simpler 3 Series in the 2027 lineup.


Since the E46, more power hasn’t necessarily made us like a given 3 Series variant more. We have a deep appreciation for cars that bring joy to our everyday lives by balancing accessible performance with real-world comfort, and that means we often care more about suspension tuning than power output. BMW’s modern turbo fours have delivered plenty of power for a sporty, entry-level luxury sedan. Even better, their chassis have avoided the “stiffer is sportier” trend of recent M cars. Our staff also includes some huge fans of straight-sixes, such as site director and Z3 2.5 owner Eric Weiner, who is a self-described fan of a 340i with a Track Pack, or perhaps a performance-pack M340i.

BMW

BMW


Despite the radical styling updates, which we’ll discuss in a minute, the powertrains for the eighth-generation 3 Series are familiar. For starters, the entry-level model uses a 2.0-liter, turbocharged inline-four with a mild-hybrid system that makes 255 hp and 295 lb-ft of torque—[the same figures as the 2025 330i, and the 2022 330i before it](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2025-bmw-3-series-interior-tweaks-new-powertrains-and-more/) . The next step up (among the gas-powered models) is the inline-six-powered car, now called the M350 xDrive (rather than M340i). While the six-cylinder received a slight increase in power for 2025, the increase for 2027 is significant: The turbocharged inline-six now makes 437 hp, up from 386 hp. Weight has gone up along with power: *[Car and Driver](https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a73930982/2027-bmw-3-series-2026-bmw-3-series-specs-compared/)* reports a 181-pound increase from 3988 pounds to 4169 pounds for the six-cylinder car.


Besides those nominal power-to-weight ratio changes, other factors that will affect the driving experience include a new steering ratio and an upgraded brake system: BMW promises “consistent pedal feel, precise modulation, and refined acoustic performance.” BMW has also revised the suspension geometry. In front, the 2027 3 Series has more (positive) caster trail to improve handling precision and steering feel, and less camber. The five-link rear axle has more camber and stiffer chassis mounts, along with “newly developed lift-related dampers.” The standard 18-inch wheel option is gone: The wheel and tire packages include 19- and 20-inch staggered diameters and widths of 245 mm in front and 255 mm in rear.


BMW


We’d be remiss, of course, if we didn’t touch on styling. While we appreciated that the current-gen 3 wasn’t burdened by the beaver-tooth aggression of the M products, the overall language of the eighth-gen cars was nonetheless long in the tooth. We’re excited that BMW’s product planners took a holistic approach with the new car, and that it evolves the 3’s brand without resorting to gimmicks or gaping maws. The kidneys are smaller—finally—while the angle of the lights at the front and rear give the car an entirely different, more cross-eyed expression from either end. Inside, BMW has doubled down on the screen-forward approach, pairing an angular touchscreen on the dash with a curved display spanning the dash closer to the windshield (essentially, it replaces the instrument cluster).

All that said, a good sport sedan’s character shouldn’t hinge on the size of the infotainment screen or the angle of its DRLs. How will it stack up against Cadillac’s aging-but-good CT4 and the perennial favorite Integra Type S in terms of driving dynamics? That’s what we’re dying to find out. The base 2027 3 Series, the 330, costs $51,250, about $2K below the average price of a new car (as of this writing and per *[Automotive News](https://www.autonews.com/)* ). We love a sedan that hits the perfect middle ground of sportiness and livability at a reasonable price, and we can’t wait to get behind the wheel of the new 3 Series.
